question: A developer building a Python Agent SDK application wants to load a SessionStart hook that resets telemetry state at the beginning of every session. They discover the Python HookEvent type does not include SessionStart as a registrable SDK callback. What should they do to still run this logic?
options: A) Define the hook as a shell command hook in .claude/settings.json and load it via setting_sources=["project"] in ClaudeAgentOptions
B) Use PostCompact as a substitute, since it is functionally equivalent to SessionStart in the Python SDK
C) Switch the entire application to TypeScript, since Python cannot run any initialization logic at session start under any configuration
D) Register the logic under PreToolUse instead, since PreToolUse fires before SessionStart in the Python SDK's internal event order
correct_answers: A) Define the hook as a shell command hook in .claude/settings.json and load it via setting_sources=["project"] in ClaudeAgentOptions
explanations: Correct. SessionStart and SessionEnd aren't available as SDK callback hooks in Python, but they can be defined as shell command hooks in settings files; enabling setting_sources=["project"] loads .claude/settings.json, including its hooks.
Incorrect. PostCompact fires after context compaction, an unrelated lifecycle event, and is not a substitute for session-start initialization.
Incorrect. A full language migration is unnecessary; Python can still run SessionStart logic via shell command hooks loaded from settings files.
Incorrect. PreToolUse fires only before tool calls, not at session initialization, and there is no documented ordering that makes it substitute for SessionStart.
